63: sealed class Screen(val route: String, val title: String, val icon: ImageVector) {

65:     object Servers : Screen("servers", "MCP Servers", Icons.Default.Hub)

67:     object Settings : Screen("settings", "Settings", Icons.Default.Settings)

70: /** Sub-routes pushed on top of the bottom-bar destinations. */
71: private const val SERVER_ADD_ROUTE = "servers/add"
72: private const val SERVER_EDIT_ROUTE = "servers/edit/{serverId}"
73: private fun serverEditRoute(serverId: String) = "servers/edit/$serverId"
74: 
75: private const val PROVIDERS_ROUTE = "providers"
76: private const val PROVIDER_EDIT_ROUTE = "providers/edit?configId={configId}&presetType={presetType}"
77: private fun providerAddRoute(presetType: String) = "providers/edit?presetType=$presetType"
78: private fun providerEditRoute(configId: String) = "providers/edit?configId=$configId"

80: @AndroidEntryPoint
81: class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
82:     override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
83:         super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
84:         enableEdgeToEdge()
85:         setContent {
86:             val themeViewModel: ThemeViewModel = hiltViewModel()
87:             val prefs by themeViewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
88:             val systemDark = isSystemInDarkTheme()
89:             val darkTheme = when (prefs.themeMode) {
90:                 ThemeMode.LIGHT -> false
91:                 ThemeMode.DARK -> true
92:                 ThemeMode.SYSTEM -> systemDark
93:             }
94:             MyApplicationTheme(
95:                 darkTheme = darkTheme,
96:                 dynamicColor = prefs.useDynamicColor,
97:                 useAmoledDark = prefs.useAmoledDark,
98:             ) {
99:                 MainApp()
100:             }
101:         }
102:     }
103: }

105: @Composable
106: fun MainApp() {
107:     val context = LocalContext.current
108:     var showOnboarding by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
109:     androidx.compose.runtime.LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
110:         showOnboarding = !hasSeenOnboarding(context)
111:     }
112:     val navController = rememberNavController()
113: 
114:     val navBackStackEntry by navController.currentBackStackEntryAsState()

134:     Scaffold(

152:                                 selectedTextColor = IndigoPrimary,

155:                                 unselectedTextColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
156:                             ),

162:                                             saveState = true
163:                                         }

166:                                     }
167:                                 }
168:                             },
169:                         )
170:                     }
171:                 }
172:             }
173:         },
174:         modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),

178:             startDestination = Screen.Chat.route,
179:             enterTransition = { fadeIn() + slideInVertically(initialOffsetY = { it / 40 }) },
180:             exitTransition = { fadeOut() + slideOutVertically(targetOffsetY = { it / 40 }) },
181:             modifier = Modifier.padding(innerPadding),
182:         ) {
183:             composable(Screen.Chat.route) {
184:                 val chatViewModel: com.aistudio.mcpchat.ui.viewmodel.ChatViewModel = hiltViewModel()

198:                 )
199:             }
200:             composable(Screen.Servers.route) {

234:                     },

But wait — `scrollBehavior = scrollBehavior` is a named parameter. In Kotlin, for a named parameter to be recognized, it needs to be placed correctly in the parameter list. TopAppBar signature is something like:
```kotlin
@Composable
fun TopAppBar(
    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    navigationIcon: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null,
    actions: @Composable (RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    scrollBehavior: TopAppBarScrollBehavior? = null,
    colors: TopAppBarColors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(),
    // ...
)
```

Wait — in material3 1.3.x, is `scrollBehavior` before or after `colors`? Let me think. I believe the parameter order in recent material3 is:
`TopAppBar(title, modifier, navigationIcon, actions, scrollBehavior, windowInsets, colors)` — actually I recall in 1.3.0, the parameter order changed. But using named arguments `scrollBehavior = scrollBehavior` works regardless of position. Yes, named args are position-independent. So my edits are fine.

1: package com.aistudio.mcpchat.data.model
2: 
3: import org.json.JSONObject
4: 
5: /**
6:  * Encodes/decodes the HTTP headers an MCP server requires.
7:  *
8:  * Storage format: a JSON object of header name → value, e.g.
9:  * `{"Authorization":"Bearer x","X-API-Key":"y"}`. Values written before this
10:  * codec existed keep working as a single header: "Name: value" splits on the
11:  * first colon, anything else becomes the Authorization header value.
12:  */
13: object McpHeaderCodec {
14: 
15:     fun encode(headers: Map<String, String>): String {
16:         val valid = headers.filterKeys { it.isNotBlank() }
17:         if (valid.isEmpty()) return ""
18:         return JSONObject()
19:             .apply { valid.forEach { (name, value) -> put(name, value) } }
20:             .toString()
21:     }
22: 
23:     fun decode(raw: String): Map<String, String> {
24:         val value = raw.trim()
25:         if (value.isEmpty()) return emptyMap()
26: 
27:         if (value.startsWith("{")) {
28:             try {
29:                 val obj = JSONObject(value)
30:                 return buildMap {
31:                     obj.keys().forEach { key ->
32:                         val name = key.trim()
33:                         if (name.isNotEmpty()) put(name, obj.getString(key).trim())
34:                     }
35:                 }
36:             } catch (_: Exception) {
37:                 // Corrupt JSON — fall through to single-header handling.
38:             }
39:         }
40:         return singleHeader(value)
41:     }
42: 
43:     private fun singleHeader(value: String): Map<String, String> {
44:         val parts = value.split(":", limit = 2)
45:         val name = parts[0].trim()
46:         return if (parts.size == 2 && isValidHeaderName(name)) {
47:             mapOf(name to parts[1].trim())
48:         } else {
49:             // Bare value: "Bearer x" or ERPNext-style "token key:secret" whose
50:             // colon belongs to the VALUE, not a name separator — the whole
51:             // string is the Authorization value.
52:             mapOf("Authorization" to value)
53:         }
54:     }
55: 
56:     private fun isValidHeaderName(name: String): Boolean = name.isNotEmpty() && HEADER_NAME_REGEX.matches(name)
57: 
58:     // RFC 7230 token chars — no spaces/separators, so "token 4ed7…" (ERPNext)
59:     // fails the check and its colon is kept as part of the value.
60:     private val HEADER_NAME_REGEX = Regex("[!#$%&'*+\\-.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z]+")
61: }

343:         for (fc in functionCalls) {
344:             // Gemini receives sanitized names; resolve the original MCP tool.
345:             val originalToolName = toolNameToToolMap[fc.name]?.name
346:                 ?: sanitizedToOriginalName[fc.name]
347:             val toolDef = originalToolName?.let { toolNameToToolMap[it] }
348:             val server = toolDef?.let { def -> serverMap[def.serverId] }
349: 
350:             val toolCallId = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
351:             val toolCall = McpToolCall(
352:                 callId = toolCallId,
353:                 serverId = server?.id ?: "unknown",
354:                 serverName = server?.name ?: "Remote MCP Server",
355:                 toolName = originalToolName ?: fc.name,
356:                 inputArguments = fc.args,
357:                 status = ToolExecutionStatus.EXECUTING,
358:                 thoughtSignature = fc.thoughtSignature,
359:             )
360: 
361:             accumulatedToolCalls.add(toolCall)
362:             onToolCallUpdate?.invoke(accumulatedToolCalls)
363: 
364:             // Guard unknown tool (provider hallucinated a name or server was disabled
365:             // after tool discovery) — fail fast without calling MCP over an empty endpoint.
366:             val resolvedToolName = originalToolName ?: fc.name
367:             val (execResult, logItem) = if (server == null) {
368:                 val errorJson = JSONObject().put("error", "Unknown tool '$resolvedToolName' — no enabled MCP server provides this tool").toString()
369:                 val syntheticLog = McpLogItem(
370:                     serverId = "unknown",
371:                     serverName = "Unknown",
372:                     toolName = resolvedToolName,
373:                     requestPayload = JSONObject().apply {
374:                         put("name", resolvedToolName)
375:                         put("arguments", JSONObject(fc.args))
376:                     }.toString(2),
377:                     responsePayload = errorJson,
378:                     isSuccess = false,
379:                     latencyMs = 0,
380:                     errorMessage = "Unknown tool",
381:                 )
382:                 errorJson to syntheticLog
383:             } else {
384:                 mcpRepository.executeTool(
385:                     server,
386:                     resolvedToolName,
387:                     fc.args,
388:                 )
389:             }
390: 
391:             replaceToolCall(
392:                 accumulatedToolCalls,
393:                 toolCallId,
394:                 toolCall.copy(
395:                     outputResult = execResult,
396:                     isSuccess = logItem.isSuccess,
397:                     status = if (logItem.isSuccess) ToolExecutionStatus.SUCCESS else ToolExecutionStatus.ERROR,
398:                     executionTimeMs = logItem.latencyMs,
399:                     errorMessage = logItem.errorMessage,
400:                 ),
401:             )
402:             onToolCallUpdate?.invoke(accumulatedToolCalls)
403: 
404:             // Build function response payload for next turn
405:             functionResponsesParts.add(
406:                 GeminiPart.FunctionResponse(
407:                     name = fc.name,
408:                     response = parseResultToMap(execResult),
409:                     thoughtSignature = fc.thoughtSignature,
410:                 ),
411:             )
412:         }
413:         return functionResponsesParts
414:     }
415: 
416:     private fun replaceToolCall(accumulatedToolCalls: MutableList<McpToolCall>, callId: String, updated: McpToolCall) {
417:         val index = accumulatedToolCalls.indexOfFirst { it.callId == callId }
418:         if (index >= 0) {
419:             accumulatedToolCalls[index] = updated
420:         }
421:     }
422: 
423:     private fun parseResultToMap(execResult: String): Map<String, Any?> {
424:         return try {
425:             val jsonObj = JSONObject(execResult)
426:             buildMap {
427:                 val keys = jsonObj.keys()
428:                 while (keys.hasNext()) {
429:                     val k = keys.next()
430:                     put(k, jsonObj.get(k))
431:                 }
432:             }
433:         } catch (_: Exception) {
434:             mapOf("result" to (if (execResult.isNotBlank()) execResult.take(1000) else "Empty response"))
435:         }
436:     }
437: 
438:     private fun serializeToolCalls(calls: List<McpToolCall>): String {
439:         val array = JSONArray()
440:         for (c in calls) {
441:             val obj = JSONObject().apply {
442:                 put("callId", c.callId)
443:                 put("serverId", c.serverId)
444:                 put("serverName", c.serverName)
445:                 put("toolName", c.toolName)
446:                 put("inputArguments", JSONObject(c.inputArguments))
447:                 put("outputResult", c.outputResult ?: "")
448:                 put("isSuccess", c.isSuccess)
449:                 put("executionTimeMs", c.executionTimeMs)
450:                 put("status", c.status.name)
451:                 put("thoughtSignature", c.thoughtSignature ?: JSONObject.NULL)
452:                 put("errorMessage", c.errorMessage ?: "")
453:                 put("timestamp", c.timestamp)
454:             }
455:             array.put(obj)
456:         }
457:         return array.toString()
458:     }
459: 
460:     fun parseToolCallsJson(jsonStr: String): List<McpToolCall> {
461:         val list = mutableListOf<McpToolCall>()

463:             val array = JSONArray(jsonStr)
464:             for (i in 0 until array.length()) {

466:                 val argsObj = obj.optJSONObject("inputArguments") ?: JSONObject()
467:                 val argsMap = mutableMapOf<String, Any?>()

470:                     val k = keys.next()
471:                     argsMap[k] = argsObj.get(k)
472:                 }
473: 
474:                 list.add(
475:                     McpToolCall(
476:                         callId = obj.optString("callId", UUID.randomUUID().toString()),
477:                         serverId = obj.optString("serverId", "unknown"),
478:                         serverName = obj.optString("serverName", "Remote MCP Server"),
479:                         toolName = obj.optString("toolName", "tool"),
480:                         inputArguments = argsMap,
481:                         outputResult = obj.optString("outputResult").takeIf { it.isNotBlank() },
482:                         isSuccess = obj.optBoolean("isSuccess", true),
483:                         executionTimeMs = obj.optLong("executionTimeMs", 0),
484:                         status = try {
485:                             ToolExecutionStatus.valueOf(obj.optString("status", "SUCCESS"))
486:                         } catch (_: Exception) {
487:                             ToolExecutionStatus.SUCCESS
488:                         },
489:                         thoughtSignature = obj.optString("thoughtSignature", null).takeIf { it != "null" },
490:                         errorMessage = obj.optString("errorMessage").takeIf { it.isNotBlank() },
491:                         timestamp = obj.optLong("timestamp", System.currentTimeMillis()),
492:                     ),
493:                 )
494:             }
495:         } catch (e: Exception) {

15: /**
16:  * Stores the user-configured AI provider endpoints (including API keys) in
17:  * hardware-backed encrypted preferences. A build-time key from `.env`
18:  * (`BuildConfig.GEMINI_API_KEY`) only seeds the Google preset on first run;
19:  * it is written straight into the encrypted store and everything the user
20:  * edits afterwards lives in encrypted prefs only.

22:  * The prefs implementation is injectable so JVM tests can supply an
23:  * in-memory map (EncryptedSharedPreferences itself needs AndroidKeyStore).

25: class AiProviderSettings(
26:     context: Context,
27:     prefsFactory: (Context) -> SharedPreferences = ::createEncryptedPrefs,
28: ) : com.aistudio.mcpchat.data.network.ActiveAiProviderSource {
29: 
30:     private val prefs: SharedPreferences = prefsFactory(context)
31: 
32:     // -- Reads ------------------------------------------------------------
33: 
34:     @Synchronized
35:     fun getAll(): List<AiProviderConfig> = decode(prefs.getString(KEY_PROVIDERS, null))
36: 
37:     @Synchronized
38:     fun getActiveId(): String = prefs.getString(KEY_ACTIVE_ID, null)
39:         ?: AiProviderIds.ID_GOOGLE
40: 
41:     @Synchronized
42:     override fun getActive(): AiProviderConfig {
43:         val all = getAll()
44:         return all.find { it.id == activeIdSafe() }
45:             ?: all.find { it.id == AiProviderIds.ID_GOOGLE }
46:             ?: all.firstOrNull()
47:             ?: AiProviderConfig.google()
48:     }
49: 
50:     // -- Writes -----------------------------------------------------------
51: 
52:     @Synchronized
53:     fun upsert(config: AiProviderConfig) {
54:         val others = getAll().filterNot { it.id == config.id }
55:         val updated = others + config
56:         prefs.edit()
57:             .putString(KEY_PROVIDERS, encode(updated))
58:             .apply()
59:     }
60: 
61:     @Synchronized
62:     fun setActive(id: String) {
63:         prefs.edit().putString(KEY_ACTIVE_ID, id).apply()
64:     }
65: 
66:     @Synchronized
67:     fun delete(id: String) {
68:         val remaining = getAll().filterNot { it.id == id }
69:         prefs.edit().putString(KEY_PROVIDERS, encode(remaining)).apply()
70:         if (getActiveId() == id) {
71:             prefs.edit()
72:                 .putString(KEY_ACTIVE_ID, remaining.firstOrNull()?.id ?: AiProviderIds.ID_GOOGLE)
73:                 .apply()

75:     }

79:     private fun activeIdSafe(): String = prefs.getString(KEY_ACTIVE_ID, null) ?: AiProviderIds.ID_GOOGLE
80: 
81:     private fun encode(configs: List<AiProviderConfig>): String {
82:         val array = JSONArray()
83:         configs.forEach { config ->
84:             array.put(
85:                 JSONObject().apply {
86:                     put("id", config.id)
87:                     put("name", config.name)
88:                     put("type", config.type.name)
89:                     put("baseUrl", config.baseUrl)
90:                     put("apiKey", config.apiKey)
91:                     put("model", config.model)
92:                 },
93:             )
94:         }
95:         return array.toString()
96:     }
97: 
98:     private fun decode(raw: String?): List<AiProviderConfig> {
99:         if (raw.isNullOrBlank()) return defaultPresets()
100:         return try {
101:             val array = JSONArray(raw)
102:             (0 until array.length()).mapNotNull { i ->
103:                 val obj = array.getJSONObject(i)
104:                 AiProviderConfig(
105:                     id = obj.optString("id"),
106:                     name = obj.optString("name"),
107:                     type = runCatching {
108:                         AiProviderType.valueOf(obj.optString("type"))
109:                     }.getOrDefault(AiProviderType.OPENAI_COMPATIBLE),
110:                     baseUrl = obj.optString("baseUrl"),
111:                     apiKey = obj.optString("apiKey"),
112:                     model = obj.optString("model"),
113:                 )
114:             }
115:         } catch (_: Exception) {
116:             defaultPresets()
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     /** First-run seed so chat works out of the box with Google + placeholders. */
121:     private fun defaultPresets(): List<AiProviderConfig> {
122:         val presets = listOf(
123:             AiProviderConfig.google(apiKey = buildTimeGeminiKey()),
124:             AiProviderConfig.anthropic(),
125:             AiProviderConfig.openAi(),
126:             AiProviderConfig.openCode(),
127:             AiProviderConfig.groq(),
128:             AiProviderConfig.openRouter(),
129:             AiProviderConfig.ollama(),
130:         )
131:         if (prefs.getString(KEY_PROVIDERS, null) == null) {
132:             prefs.edit()
133:                 .putString(KEY_PROVIDERS, encode(presets))
134:                 .putString(KEY_ACTIVE_ID, AiProviderIds.ID_GOOGLE)
135:                 .apply()
136:         }
137:         return presets
138:     }
139: 
140:     /**
141:      * The `.env` `GEMINI_API_KEY` (injected via the secrets Gradle plugin)
142:      * seeds the Google preset on first run so a development build works
143:      * without manual key entry. The key is immediately persisted into the
144:      * encrypted prefs; later runtime edits happen in-app only. The
145:      * placeholder template value is treated as "not configured".
146:      */
147:     private fun buildTimeGeminiKey(): String {
148:         val key = BuildConfig.GEMINI_API_KEY.trim()
149:         return if (key.isEmpty() || key == MY_GEMINI_API_KEY_PLACEHOLDER) "" else key
150:     }
151: 
152:     companion object {
153:         private const val KEY_PROVIDERS = "ai_providers"
154:         private const val KEY_ACTIVE_ID = "ai_provider_active"
155:         private const val MY_GEMINI_API_KEY_PLACEHOLDER = "MY_GEMINI_API_KEY"
156: 
157:         fun createEncryptedPrefs(context: Context): SharedPreferences =
158:             createEncryptedPrefs(context, allowPlaintextFallback = ::isRuntimeWithoutKeystore)
159: 
160:         /**
161:          * Opens the encrypted prefs, deciding via [allowPlaintextFallback]
162:          * whether a failure may degrade to plaintext storage. Production
163:          * must never silently store API keys unencrypted, so the default
164:          * ([isRuntimeWithoutKeystore]) only permits the fallback under
165:          * Robolectric / stubbed android.jar where no AndroidKeyStore exists.
166:          */
167:         internal fun createEncryptedPrefs(context: Context, allowPlaintextFallback: () -> Boolean): SharedPreferences {
168:             return try {
169:                 val masterKey = MasterKey.Builder(context)
170:                     .setKeyScheme(MasterKey.KeyScheme.AES256_GCM)
171:                     .build()
172: 
173:                 EncryptedSharedPreferences.create(
174:                     context,
175:                     "ai_provider_prefs",
176:                     masterKey,
177:                     EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefKeyEncryptionScheme.AES256_SIV,
178:                     EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefValueEncryptionScheme.AES256_GCM,
179:                 )
180:             } catch (e: Exception) {
181:                 if (!allowPlaintextFallback()) {
182:                     throw IllegalStateException(
183:                         "EncryptedSharedPreferences is unavailable on this device; " +
184:                             "refusing to store provider API keys in plaintext",
185:                         e,
186:                     )
187:                 }
188:                 context.getSharedPreferences("ai_provider_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
189:             }
190:         }
191: 
192:         /**
193:          * Robolectric reports a "robolectric" fingerprint; the mockable
194:          * android.jar used by plain JVM tests leaves statics null. A real
195:          * device always has a genuine non-empty fingerprint.
196:          */
197:         private fun isRuntimeWithoutKeystore(): Boolean {
198:             val fingerprint = Build.FINGERPRINT
199:             return fingerprint.isNullOrEmpty() || fingerprint.startsWith("robolectric")
200:         }
201:     }

14: /**
15:  * Encrypts short secrets (MCP server auth headers) at rest using AES/GCM
16:  * backed by the Android Keystore.
17:  *
18:  * Ciphertext format: "enc:v1:<base64 iv>:<base64 ciphertext>". Values without
19:  * that prefix are treated as legacy plaintext so existing rows keep working;
20:  * they are re-encrypted transparently on the next write.
21:  */
22: class CryptoManager(
23:     private val keyProvider: () -> SecretKey = { getOrCreateKeystoreKey() },
24: ) {
25: 
26:     fun encrypt(plain: String): String {
27:         if (plain.isBlank()) return plain
28:         if (plain.startsWith(PREFIX)) return plain // already encrypted
29: 
30:         val cipher = Cipher.getInstance(TRANSFORMATION)
31:         cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, keyProvider())
32:         val iv = cipher.iv
33:         val encrypted = cipher.doFinal(plain.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
34: 
35:         val encodedIv = iv.toByteString().base64()
36:         val encodedData = encrypted.toByteString().base64()
37:         return "$PREFIX$VERSION:$encodedIv:$encodedData"
38:     }
39: 
40:     @Suppress("ThrowsCount")
41:     fun decrypt(value: String): String {
42:         if (value.isBlank()) return value
43:         if (!value.startsWith(PREFIX)) return value // legacy plaintext
44: 
45:         val parts = value.removePrefix(PREFIX).split(":", limit = 3)
46:         require(parts.size == 3 && parts[0] == VERSION) { "Unsupported ciphertext format" }
47: 
48:         val iv = parts[1].decodeBase64()?.toByteArray()
49:             ?: throw IllegalArgumentException("Corrupted ciphertext IV")
50:         val encrypted = parts[2].decodeBase64()?.toByteArray()
51:             ?: throw IllegalArgumentException("Corrupted ciphertext payload")
52: 
53:         val cipher = Cipher.getInstance(TRANSFORMATION)
54:         cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, keyProvider(), GCMParameterSpec(GCM_TAG_LENGTH_BITS, iv))
55:         return String(cipher.doFinal(encrypted), Charsets.UTF_8)
56:     }
57: 
58:     companion object {
59:         private const val PREFIX = "enc:"
60:         private const val VERSION = "v1"
61:         private const val TRANSFORMATION = "AES/GCM/NoPadding"
62:         private const val GCM_TAG_LENGTH_BITS = 128
63: 
64:         private const val KEYSTORE = "AndroidKeyStore"
65:         private const val KEY_ALIAS = "mcp_chat_auth_header_key"
66: 
67:         /**

69:          * Android runtime; callers on JVM test environments inject their own
70:          * [SecretKey] via the constructor instead.
71:          */
72:         private fun getOrCreateKeystoreKey(): SecretKey {
73:             val keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance(KEYSTORE).apply { load(null) }
74:             (keyStore.getKey(KEY_ALIAS, null) as? SecretKey)?.let { return it }
75: 
76:             val generator = KeyGenerator.getInstance(KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_AES, KEYSTORE)

80:             )
81:                 .setBlockModes(KeyProperties.BLOCK_MODE_GCM)

90:                 .build()

277:         private val allowedSchemaKeys =

289:         fun sanitizeSchema(schema: JSONObject): JSONObject {

292:                 if (key !in allowedSchemaKeys) continue
293:                 when (key) {
294:                     "type" -> sanitized.put("type", normalizeType(schema.optString(key)))
295:                     "properties" -> sanitized.put("properties", sanitizeProperties(schema.optJSONObject(key)))
296:                     "items" -> {

303:                 }
304:             }
305:             if (!sanitized.has("type")) {
306:                 // Gemini rejects property schemas without an explicit type.
307:                 if (sanitized.has("properties") || sanitized.has("required")) {
308:                     sanitized.put("type", "OBJECT")

312:             }
313:             return sanitized

317:             val cleanProperties = JSONObject()
318:             if (properties == null) return cleanProperties
319:             for (propKey in properties.keys()) {
320:                 val propObj = properties.optJSONObject(propKey) ?: continue
321:                 cleanProperties.put(propKey, sanitizeSchema(propObj))
322:             }
323:             return cleanProperties
324:         }

331:                 "boolean" -> "BOOLEAN"
332:                 "array" -> "ARRAY"

1. **`AiChatService` interface** — add streaming method with default fallback:

```kotlin
interface AiChatService {
    suspend fun generateContent(...): GeminiResponse

    suspend fun streamContent(
        config: AiProviderConfig,
        modelName: String,
        history: List<GeminiMessage>,
        tools: List<McpTool>,
        systemInstruction: String,
        onTextDelta: (String) -> Unit,
    ): GeminiResponse {
        // Default fallback: non-streaming, emit whole text as one delta
        val response = generateContent(config, modelName, history, tools, systemInstruction)
        response.text?.let(onTextDelta)
        return response
    }
}
```

Wait, but `OpenAiCompatibleClient` and `AnthropicClient` don't implement `AiChatService`! Looking at the code:
- `GeminiApiService : AiChatService`
- `OpenAiCompatibleClient` — plain class, no interface
- `AnthropicClient` — plain class, no interface
- `ProviderChatRouter : AiChatService` routes to them

Interesting — only Gemini and Router implement the interface. OpenAI/Anthropic clients are duck-typed. OK, I'll add `streamContent` to all three classes + the Router + the interface.

2. **SSE parsing** — custom parser. SSE format:
```
data: {...json...}

data: {...json...}
```
Lines starting with `data:` (optionally followed by space) accumulate; blank line dispatches event. Also `event:` and `id:` fields, comments start with `:`. For all three providers, we only need `data:` lines.

I'll create a shared helper in `OkHttpExtensions.kt` or a new `SseParser.kt`:

```kotlin
/**
 * Reads an SSE (`text/event-stream`) response body and invokes [onEvent] for
 * each `data:` field. Returns when the stream ends.
 */
suspend fun Response.readSseEvents(onEvent: (String) -> Unit) {
    val source = body?.source() ?: return
    val dataBuffer = StringBuilder()
    while (true) {
        val line = source.readUtf8Line() ?: break  // EOF
        when {
            line.isEmpty() -> {
                if (dataBuffer.isNotEmpty()) {
                    onEvent(dataBuffer.toString())
                    dataBuffer.setLength(0)
                }
            }
            line.startsWith("data:") -> {
                val data = line.removePrefix("data:").removePrefix(" ").also ...
                // multi-line data: append with \n per SSE spec

3. **Gemini streaming** (`streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`):

URL: `$baseUrl/$targetModel:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`
Body: same as generateContent.
SSE events: each `data:` is a JSON GenerateContentResponse chunk:
```json
{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"text":"Hello"}]}}]}
```
Function calls arrive as `{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{...}}]}}]}` — complete in one part typically. I'll accumulate text parts → emit deltas; accumulate functionCalls; final response = accumulated.

Implementation:
```kotlin
suspend fun streamContent(...onTextDelta: (String) -> Unit): GeminiResponse = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    // key check same as generateContent
    val requestJson = buildRequestBody(...) // reuse
    val url = "$baseUrl/$targetModel:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse"
    val request = ... same headers
    try {
        client.newCall(request).await().use { response ->
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                return@use errorResponse(modelName, response.code, response.body?.string() ?: "")
            }
            val textBuilder = StringBuilder()
            val functionCalls = mutableListOf<GeminiPart.FunctionCall>()
            response.readSseEvents { data ->
                try {
                    val json = JSONObject(data)
                    val parts = json.optJSONArray("candidates")?.optJSONObject(0)
                        ?.optJSONObject("content")?.optJSONArray("parts") ?: return@readSseEvents
                    for (i in 0 until parts.length()) {
                        val part = parts.getJSONObject(i)
                        if (part.has("text")) {
                            val text = part.getString("text")
                            textBuilder.append(text)
                            onTextDelta(text)
                        }
                        if (part.has("functionCall")) functionCalls.add(parseFunctionCall(part))
                    }
                } catch (_: Exception) { /* skip malformed chunk */ }
            }
            GeminiResponse(
                text = textBuilder.toString().takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() },
                functionCalls = functionCalls,
                rawJson = "",
            )
        }
    } catch (CancellationException) throw ... same error handling
}
```

**1. SSE parser in OkHttpExtensions.kt:**

```kotlin
/**
 * Parses a Server-Sent Events (SSE) body and invokes [onData] with each
 * complete `data:` field value. Blocks the current thread reading lines —
 * call from Dispatchers.IO. Cancellation of the coroutine closes the
 * response via Call.cancel() and the read throws.
 */
fun Response.forEachSseData(onData: (String) -> Unit) {
    val source = body?.source() ?: return
    val buffer = StringBuilder()
    while (true) {
        val line = try {
            source.readUtf8Line() ?: break // EOF ends the stream
        } catch (e: IOException) {
            if (call().isCanceled()) throw e // surfaced as cancellation upstream
            throw e
        }
        when {
            line.isEmpty() -> {
                if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) {
                    onData(buffer.toString())
                    buffer.setLength(0)
                }
            }
            line.startsWith("data:") -> {
                var data = line.removePrefix("data:")
                if (data.startsWith(" ")) data = data.removePrefix(" ")
                if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) buffer.append('\n')
                buffer.append(data)
            }
            // `event:`, `id:`, `retry:` and `:comments` carry no payload for
            // the AI providers — ignored.
        }
    }
    // Flush a trailing event that was not terminated by a blank line.
    if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) onData(buffer.toString())
}
```

Hmm wait — the IOException handling: if call was cancelled, the IOException from the closed socket propagates up. In the client's catch clauses: `catch (e: IOException)` → returns GeminiResponse(error="unreachable..."). But if the coroutine was CANCELLED, the correct behavior is to propagate CancellationException. The existing await() handles cancellation: `continuation.cancel(e)` — but that only applies while awaiting. After await() resumed, cancellation invokes call.cancel(), and my read throws IOException. The catch would swallow it into an error response, BUT withContext(Dispatchers.IO) checks cancellation on exit — the coroutine IS cancelled, so withContext throws CancellationException regardless of the block's return value. 

Hmm, actually — is that true? `withContext` on cancellation: "If the coroutine is cancelled while withContext is executing, withContext throws CancellationException when the block completes". Yes — kotlinx.coroutines withContext is cancellable at completion: it checks the job state before resuming the caller. Even if the block returns normally, withContext throws CancellationException if the job was cancelled. So Stop works correctly.

But to be extra safe and clean, in the catch-clause chain of my streaming methods I'll mirror the existing pattern (rethrow CancellationException first, catch IOException → error response). The IOException-from-cancel path still ends in CancellationException thanks to withContext exit check. 

One more consideration — `readUtf8Line()` vs timeouts: read timeout (60s default client; the AI providers client) applies per read operation. Long thinking pauses > 60s → SocketTimeoutException (a subclass of IOException) → error response "unreachable: timeout". Existing behavior parity (non-streaming would also time out). OK.

interface AiChatService {
    suspend fun generateContent(...): GeminiResponse

    /**
     * Streaming variant: emits partial text via [onTextDelta] as tokens
     * arrive and returns the complete response (including any function
     * calls) once the stream ends. Default falls back to non-streaming and
     * emits the whole text as a single delta.
     */
    suspend fun streamContent(
        config: AiProviderConfig,
        modelName: String,
        history: List<GeminiMessage>,
        tools: List<McpTool>,
        systemInstruction: String,
        onTextDelta: (String) -> Unit,
    ): GeminiResponse {
        val response = generateContent(config, modelName, history, tools, systemInstruction)
        response.text?.let { onTextDelta(it) }
        return response
    }
}

```kotlin
override suspend fun streamContent(
    config, modelName, history, tools, systemInstruction,
    onTextDelta: (String) -> Unit,
): GeminiResponse = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    val apiKey = config.apiKey.trim()
    if (apiKey.isBlank() || apiKey == "MY_GEMINI_API_KEY") {
        return@withContext GeminiResponse(text = null, error = "API_KEY_MISSING")
    }
    try {
        val requestJson = buildRequestBody(history, tools, systemInstruction)
        val targetModel = if (modelName.contains("/")) modelName else "models/$modelName"
        val baseUrl = config.baseUrl.trimEnd('/').ifBlank { "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta" }
        val url = "$baseUrl/$targetModel:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse"
        val request = Request.Builder()...same headers...
        client.newCall(request).await().use { response ->
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                return@use errorResponse(modelName, response.code, response.body?.string() ?: "")
            }
            val text = StringBuilder()
            val functionCalls = mutableListOf<GeminiPart.FunctionCall>()
            response.forEachSseData { data ->
                parseStreamChunk(data, text, functionCalls, onTextDelta)
            }
            GeminiResponse(
                text = text.toString().takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() },
                functionCalls = functionCalls,
                rawJson = "",
            )
        }
    } catch (e: kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) {
        throw e
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        Log.e(TAG, "Exception during Gemini streamContent", e)
        GeminiResponse(text = null, error = e.message ?: "Unknown error calling Gemini API")
    }
}

private fun parseStreamChunk(data: String, textBuilder: StringBuilder, functionCalls: MutableList<GeminiPart.FunctionCall>, onTextDelta: (String) -> Unit) {
    try {
        val json = JSONObject(data)
        // Mid-stream protocol errors carry an "error" object.
        json.optJSONObject("error")?.let { err ->
            // Hmm — how to signal? Can't easily mutate the return from here.
        }
        val parts = json.optJSONArray("candidates")?.optJSONObject(0)
            ?.optJSONObject("content")?.optJSONArray("parts") ?: return
        for (i in 0 until parts.length()) {
            val partObj = parts.getJSONObject(i)
            if (partObj.has("text")) {
                val delta = partObj.getString("text")
                textBuilder.append(delta)
                onTextDelta(delta)
            }
            if (partObj.has("functionCall")) {
                functionCalls.add(parseFunctionCall(partObj))
            }
        }
    } catch (_: Exception) {
        // Malformed chunk — skip; the stream continues.
    }
}

**4. OpenAiCompatibleClient streaming:**

Chunk: `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}|{"tool_calls":[...]}, "finish_reason":...}]}`
Sentinel: `data: [DONE]`.

```kotlin
suspend fun streamContent(...onTextDelta): GeminiResponse = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    if (config.apiKey.isBlank() && requiresApiKey(config)) {
        return@withContext GeminiResponse(text = null, error = API_KEY_MISSING)
    }
    try {
        val body = buildRequestJson(config, modelName, history, tools, systemInstruction)
            .put("stream", true)
        val request = ...same as generateContent...
        client.newCall(request).await().use { response ->
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                val errorBody = response.body?.string() ?: ""
                Log.e(TAG, "OpenAI-compatible stream failed (${response.code}): $errorBody")
                return@use errorResponse(response.code, errorBody)
            }
            val text = StringBuilder()
            // tool call assembly keyed by chunk-local index
            val toolAccumulators = mutableListOf<ToolCallAccumulator>()  // or LinkedHashMap<Int, ...>
            var streamError: String? = null
            response.forEachSseData { data ->
                if (data == DONE_SENTINEL) return@forEachSseData
                try {
                    val chunk = JSONObject(data)
                    chunk.optJSONObject("error")?.let { err ->
                        streamError = err.optString("message", "stream error")
                        return@forEachSseData
                    }
                    val delta = chunk.optJSONArray("choices")?.optJSONObject(0)?.optJSONObject("delta") ?: return@forEachSseData
                    delta.optString("content").takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }?.let { piece ->
                        text.append(piece)
                        onTextDelta(piece)
                    }
                    delta.optJSONArray("tool_calls")?.let { toolCallDeltas ->
                        for (i in 0 until toolCallDeltas.length()) {
                            val tc = toolCallDeltas.getJSONObject(i)
                            val index = tc.optInt("index", 0)
                            val acc = toolAccumulators.getOrPut(index) { ToolCallAccumulator() }
                            tc.optJSONObject("function")?.let { fn ->
                                fn.optString("name").takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }?.let { acc.name = it }
                                acc.args.append(fn.optString("arguments"))
                            }
                        }
                    }
                } catch (_: Exception) { /* skip malformed chunk */ }
            }
            streamError?.let { return@use GeminiResponse(text = null, error = it) }
            val functionCalls = toolAccumulators.toSortedMap().values.mapNotNull { acc -> acc.build() }
            GeminiResponse(text = text.toString().takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }, functionCalls = functionCalls, rawJson = "")
        }
    } catch (CancellationException) throw ... etc.
}
```

With `ToolCallAccumulator` private class: `var name: String = ""; val args = StringBuilder(); fun build(): GeminiPart.FunctionCall? { if (name.isBlank()) return null; parse args JSON to map... }`

Use `LinkedHashMap<Int, ToolCallAccumulator>` — order of first appearance is index order anyway. Or `SortedMap` to be safe on ordering. I'll use LinkedHashMap and sort by key at the end — simplest: `toolAccumulators.toSortedMap()`.

Helper for args JSON → Map (reuse pattern from parseResponse):
```kotlin
private fun parseArgsMap(raw: String): MutableMap<String, Any?> {
    val args = mutableMapOf<String, Any?>()
    runCatching {
        val obj = JSONObject(raw)
        obj.keys().forEach { key -> args[key] = obj.get(key) }
    }
    return args
}
```

For `getOrPut` on a Java LinkedHashMap — Kotlin stdlib has `getOrPut` for MutableMap. Fine.

- `message_stop`

                return@use errorResponse(response.code, errorBody)
            }
            val text = StringBuilder()
            val textBlocks = sortedMapOf<Int, StringBuilder>()  // or single builder — blocks in order
            val toolBlocks = LinkedHashMap<Int, ToolUseAccumulator>()
            var stopReason: String? = null
            var streamError: String? = null
            response.forEachSseData { data ->
                try {
                    val event = JSONObject(data)
                    when (event.optString("type")) {
                        "error" -> streamError = event.optJSONObject("error")?.optString("message") ?: "stream error"
                        "content_block_start" -> {
                            val index = event.optInt("index", 0)
                            val block = event.optJSONObject("content_block") ?: return@forEachSseData
                            when (block.optString("type")) {
                                "tool_use" -> toolBlocks[index] = ToolUseAccumulator(block.optString("name"))
                                // text blocks need no state; deltas append in order
                            }
                        }
                        "content_block_delta" -> {
                            val index = event.optInt("index", 0)
                            when (val delta = event.optJSONObject("delta")) {
                                null -> Unit
                                else -> when (delta.optString("type")) {
                                    "text_delta" -> {
                                        val piece = delta.optString("text")
                                        if (piece.isNotEmpty()) { text.append(piece); onTextDelta(piece) }
                                    }
                                    "input_json_delta" -> toolBlocks[index]?.args?.append(delta.optString("partial_json"))
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        "message_delta" -> stopReason = event.optJSONObject("delta")?.optString("stop_reason")
                        // message_start/content_block_stop/message_stop: no payload needed
                    }
                } catch (_: Exception) { }
            }
            streamError?.let { return@use GeminiResponse(text = null, error = it) }
            if (stopReason == "max_tokens") text.append("\n\n[Output truncated: max_tokens reached]")
            val functionCalls = toolBlocks.entries.sortedBy { it.key }.mapNotNull { it.value.build() }
            GeminiResponse(
                text = text.toString().takeIf { it.isNotBlank() },
                functionCalls = functionCalls,
                rawJson = "",
            )
        }
    } catch ... same
}
```

}

The test uses `mockk(relaxed = true)` for ChatRepository, and stubs specific flows. The ViewModel's init now calls `chatRepository.streamEvents.collect {...}` — on a relaxed mock, `streamEvents` returns a relaxed SharedFlow mock. Collecting a mocked SharedFlow: MockK relaxed mock for `SharedFlow<ChatStreamEvent>` — when `collect` is called on it, MockK returns a relaxed default (Unit) immediately. So the collector completes without hanging. That should be fine for existing tests.

But to be explicit and safe (and for a new streaming test), I'll stub `streamEvents` in setUp:

private val streamEventsFlow = MutableSharedFlow<ChatStreamEvent>(extraBufferCapacity = 64)
...
every { chatRepository.streamEvents } returns streamEventsFlow
```
This gives a REAL flow — the collector suspends forever (normal), and I can emit events in tests. This is more deterministic than relying on relaxed mock behavior. MutableSharedFlow with no subscribers and tryEmit with extraBufferCapacity → events buffered... with extraBufferCapacity=64, tryEmit succeeds and values are retained for... no — without replay, late subscribers don't get past values. Emissions while no subscriber... hmm, MutableSharedFlow with extraBufferCapacity > 0 and no subscribers: tryEmit returns true, values are dropped immediately when there are no subscribers (they only buffer when there ARE slow subscribers).

- **Repository** — `SharedFlow<ChatStreamEvent>` (session-scoped `StreamStarted`/`TokenDelta`/`StreamFinished`, 512-slot DROP_OLDEST buffer); `StreamStarted` re-emitted per tool hop so narration resets between rounds; tool loop unchanged since function calls always arrive complete
- **ViewModel** — collects events, filters by current session (no cross-session token bleed), accumulates `streamingText` StateFlow
- **UI** — `StreamingMessageBubble` (assistant styling + pulsing dots cursor via extracted `PulsingDots`); typing indicator shows only until the first token; auto-scroll tracks token growth

/**
 * Executes the call, reads the SSE body... cancellation-safe:
 * registers on the calling job so cancel() cuts the blocking read.

suspend fun Call.awaitSse(onData: (String) -> Unit) {
    val job = currentCoroutineContext()[Job]!!
    val response = await()  // await's invokeOnCancellation covers this phase

}

Cleaner: make the extension handle the whole call:

```kotlin
/**
 * Runs [action] with the response, keeping the underlying call tied to the
 * calling job: cancelling the job (Stop button) closes the socket, which
 * interrupts the blocking SSE read and surfaces as CancellationException.
 */
suspend fun Call.executeWithJobCancellation(action: (Response) -> Unit) {
    val job = coroutineContext[Job] ?: error("no job")
    await().use { response ->
        val handle = job.invokeOnCompletion { if (it != null) cancel() }
        try {
            action(response)
        } catch (e: IOException) {
            if (isCanceled()) throw CancellationException("request cancelled", e)
            throw e
        } finally {
            handle.dispose()
        }
    }
}
```

Then clients: `client.newCall(request).executeWithJobCancellation { response -> ...existing body... }` — minimal diff! The existing body already handles non-2xx and forEachSseData.

Test sketch (AnthropicClientTest):
```kotlin
@Test
fun `cancelling mid-stream cuts the SSE read`() {
    // SSE body with several chunks, throttled
    val sseBody = ... (multiple data chunks)
    server.enqueue(MockResponse().setResponseCode(200)
        .setHeader("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        .setBody(sseBody)
        .throttleBody(1, 200, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS))  // 1 byte per 200ms → slow trickle
    
    runBlocking {
        val deltas = CopyOnWriteArrayList<String>()
        val job = launch {
            try {
                client.streamContent(config, "claude", emptyList(), emptyList(), "") { deltas.add(it) }
            } catch (e: CancellationException) {
                caught = true; throw e
            }
        }
        delay(1000) // let a few tokens arrive
        job.cancelAndJoin()
        assertTrue(deltas.isNotEmpty())  // partial tokens did arrive
        assertTrue(caught)  // surfaced as CancellationException
    }
}
```

```kotlin
suspend fun regenerateLastMessage(
    sessionId: String,
    onToolCallUpdate: ((List<McpToolCall>) -> Unit)? = null,
): Result<ChatMessageEntity> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    val session = chatDao.getSessionById(sessionId)
        ?: return@withContext Result.failure(ChatException.GeminiApi("Session no longer exists"))

    val messages = chatDao.getMessagesList(session.id)
    // Drop the trailing assistant turn so history ends at the last user message;
    // a trailing user message (stopped before any output) is retried as-is.
    messages.lastOrNull()?.takeIf { it.role == "assistant" }?.let { last ->
        chatDao.deleteMessageById(last.id)
    }
    val fallbackPrompt = messages.lastOrNull { it.role == "user" }?.content ?: ""
    generateAndPersist(session, fallbackPrompt, onToolCallUpdate)
}

suspend fun <T> Call.executeStreaming(action: (Response) -> T): T {
    val job = requireNotNull(coroutineContext[Job]) { ... }

        } finally {

}

```kotlin
@Test
fun `cancelling mid-stream interrupts the SSE body read`() {
    val sseBody = buildString {
        repeat(8) { i ->
            append("""data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":"chunk$i "}}""").append("\n\n")
        }
        append("""data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}""").append("\n\n")
        append("""data: {"type":"message_stop"}""").append("\n\n")
    }
    server.enqueue(
        MockResponse().setResponseCode(200)
            .setHeader("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
            .setBody(sseBody)
            .throttleBody(8, 100, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS),
    )

    val start = System.currentTimeMillis()
    runBlocking {
        val deltas = CopyOnWriteArrayList<String>()
        var cancellation: CancellationException? = null
        val job = launch {
            try {
                client.streamContent(config, "claude-x", emptyList(), emptyList(), "") { deltas.add(it) }
            } catch (e: CancellationException) {
                cancellation = e
                throw e
            }
        }
        delay(1200)
        job.cancelAndJoin()
        assertNotNull("expected CancellationException, got none", cancellation)
        assertTrue(deltas.isEmpty().not())
    }
    val elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis() - start
    assertTrue("cancel should interrupt the throttled read promptly (took ${elapsed}ms)", elapsed < 5000)
}

## Assistant (Code · glm-5.3 · 32.5s)

Roadmap 15.2 implemented, verified, and committed as `3ceb51e` (11 files, +454/−76).

**Mid-stream cancellation** — `Call.executeStreaming` in `OkHttpExtensions.kt:48`: the blocking SSE body read is tied to the calling job via `invokeOnCompletion` — job cancellation fires `call.cancel()`, the socket close interrupts the read, and the resulting IOException resurfaces as `CancellationException`. All three providers' `streamContent` methods migrated to it (`await()` only covered the headers phase before; the Stop button previously couldn't interrupt an in-progress body read).

**Partial response preservation** — `ChatRepository.generateAndPersist` (extracted from `sendMessage`) catches cancellation, appends a `[Generation stopped by user]` marker to the streamed partial text, persists it under `NonCancellable`, then rethrows. Stopping before any token persists no placeholder. Validated by the throttled-SSE test: a ~30s trickle body is cut in <1.6s.

**Regenerate** — `ChatDao.deleteMessageById` + `ChatRepository.regenerateLastMessage` drops the trailing assistant message (including stopped partials or errors) and re-runs generation for the last user turn; `ChatViewModel.regenerate()` and a `RegenerateAction` chip on the last message (visible when idle) wire it to the UI.

**Verification:** detekt 0 issues, spotless clean, 355 tests / 0 failures (8 new: mid-stream interrupt, partial persistence, no-op cancel, regenerate ×3, ViewModel ×2).

**Part 3: Graceful fallback to non-streaming if provider doesn't support SSE**

Currently: all clients implement streamContent with SSE. If a provider/gateway doesn't support streaming, what happens?
- Server may return 200 with Content-Type: application/json (single JSON response, not SSE) — OpenAI-compatible gateways sometimes do this when stream is unsupported/ignored, or return 400 "stream not supported".

```kotlin
data class StreamProgress(
    val elapsedMs: Long,
    val charsStreamed: Int,
    val tokensPerSecond: Int,   // rounded
    val estimatedRemainingMs: Long?,
)

class StreamProgressTracker {
    private var startMs = 0L
    private var chars = 0
    private var lastEmitMs = 0L
    private var estimatedTotalMs = DEFAULT_ESTIMATE_MS
    
    fun start(nowMs: Long) {...}
    fun onDelta(chars_: Int, nowMs: Long): StreamProgress { ... update chars; adapt estimate; compute tok/s and remaining }
    fun finish(...): null
}
```

Adaptive estimate logic:
- initial estimatedTotalMs = 12_000
- On each delta: if elapsed > estimatedTotalMs * 0.8 → estimatedTotalMs = elapsed * 1.5 (bar never quite fills; ETA grows gracefully).
- tokensPerSecond = (chars / 4f) / (elapsed/1000), using EMA of instantaneous rate for smoothness: instantaneous = deltaChars/4 / dt. EMA alpha 0.3.
- estimatedRemainingMs = (estimatedTotalMs - elapsed).coerceAtLeast(0)
- Progress fraction (for the bar) = (elapsed / estimatedTotalMs).coerceIn(0f, 0.95f) — cap below 1 so it completes only at end.

Now — **fallback detection helpers** in OkHttpExtensions.kt:

```kotlin
/** True when the response body is delivered as an SSE stream. */
fun Response.deliversSse(): Boolean =
    header("Content-Type")?.trim()?.startsWith("text/event-stream", ignoreCase = true) == true

/**
 * Heuristic for gateways that reject streaming outright (404 on the stream
 * endpoint, 501, or a 400 whose body names streaming) — retried non-streaming.
 */
fun looksLikeStreamUnsupported(code: Int, errorBody: String): Boolean =
    code == 501 || (code == 400 && errorBody.contains("stream", ignoreCase = true)) || (code == 404 && errorBody.contains("stream", ...))
```

## Assistant (Code · glm-5.3 · 25.2s)

Roadmap 15.3 implemented, verified, and committed as `60f4474` (12 files, +490/−10).

**Progress indicator** — `StreamProgressTracker` (`ui/viewmodel/StreamProgress.kt`): tokens estimated as chars/4, EMA-smoothed tok/s, and an adaptive time estimate that stretches when the stream outlives it (bar slows down but never completes early — LLM output has no known length). 100ms emit throttle keeps recomposition cheap; first delta emits immediately so the bar turns determinate right away. ChatScreen replaces the pre-token typing indicator with `StreamProgressIndicator` (indeterminate "Waiting for first token…" → determinate bar + "N tok/s · M chars · ~Xs left", live-region annotated) and renders it inside the streaming bubble. `TypingIndicator` itself is kept — it's snapshot-tested.

**Non-SSE fallback** — two detection paths in all three clients:
- 200 with non-`text/event-stream` Content-Type (gateway ignored `stream:true`/`alt=sse`): body parsed as the plain JSON response, text emitted as one delta
- Stream-rejected errors (501, or 400/404/405 naming "stream"): retried once via non-streaming `generateContent`, staying inside the job's cancellation scope since `executeStreaming`'s action is now `suspend`

**Verification:** detekt 0 issues, spotless clean, 368 tests / 0 failures (13 new: tracker math ×6, per-client fallback ×6, ViewModel progress flow ×1 — including assertions that the retry request drops `stream:true`).

@Composable
fun PendingAttachmentsBar(
    attachments: List<ImageAttachment>,
    onRemove: (ImageAttachment) -> Unit,
    onAddMore: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    LazyRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(Spacing.sm), modifier = modifier) {
        items(attachments, key = { it.uri }) { attachment ->
            Box {
                AsyncImage(
                    model = attachment.uri,
                    contentDescription = "Attached image",
                    contentScale = ContentScale.Crop,
                    modifier = Modifier.size(56.dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(Dimens.cornerRadiusSm)),
                )
                IconButton(
                    onClick = { onRemove(attachment) },
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .size(18.dp)
                        .align(Alignment.TopEnd)
                        .background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface.copy(alpha = 0.8f), CircleShape)
                        .testTag("remove_attachment_button"),
                ) {
                    Icon(Icons.Default.Close, contentDescription = "Remove attachment", modifier = Modifier.size(12.dp))
                }
            }
        }
        item(key = "add_attachment") {
            IconButton(onClick = onAddMore, modifier = Modifier.size(56.dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(Dimens.cornerRadiusSm)).background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceVariant).testTag("add_attachment_tile")) {
                Icon(Icons.Default.Add, contentDescription = "Add image")
            }
        }
    }
}

```kotlin
@Test
fun `history rebuild includes inline image parts for persisted attachments`() = runTest {
    coEvery { chatDao.getSessionById("s1") } returns ChatSessionEntity(id = "s1", title = "Test")
    coEvery { chatDao.getMessagesList("s1") } returns listOf(
        ChatMessageEntity(
            id = "m1", sessionId = "s1", role = "user", content = "what is this?",
            attachmentsJson = """[{"uri":"content://media/1","mimeType":"image/png"}]""",
        ),
    )
    val historySlot = slot<List<GeminiMessage>>()
    coEvery { geminiService.streamContent(any(), any(), capture(historySlot), any(), any(), any()) } returns
        com.aistudio.mcpchat.data.model.GeminiResponse(text = "a cat")

    val fakeSource = AttachmentContentSource {
        LoadedAttachment(mimeType = "image/png", base64Data = "aGVsbG8=")
    }
    repository = ChatRepository(database, mockk(relaxed = true), geminiService, attachmentSource = fakeSource)
    repository.sendMessage(sessionId = "s1", userPrompt = "describe")
    advanceUntilIdle()

    val userMsg = historySlot.captured.first { it.role == "user" }
    val inline = userMsg.parts.filterIsInstance<GeminiPart.InlineData>().single()
    assertEquals("image/png", inline.mimeType)
    assertEquals("aGVsbG8=", inline.base64Data)
    assertTrue(userMsg.parts.any { it is GeminiPart.Text && it.text == "what is this?" })
}
```

15:  * Suspends until the call completes. Cancelling the coroutine cancels the

18:  */
19: suspend fun Call.await(): Response = suspendCancellableCoroutine { continuation ->
20:     enqueue(
21:         object : Callback {
22:             override fun onResponse(call: Call, response: Response) {
23:                 continuation.resume(response)
24:             }
25: 
26:             override fun onFailure(call: Call, e: IOException) {
27:                 if (call.isCanceled()) {
28:                     // Surface cancellation as CancellationException so
29:                     // structured concurrency keeps working.
30:                     continuation.cancel(e)
31:                 } else {
32:                     continuation.resumeWithException(e)
33:                 }
34:             }
35:         },
36:     )
37:     continuation.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
38: }
39: 
40: /**
41:  * Executes the call and consumes the response body inside [action] with the
42:  * blocking read tied to the calling job: [await] covers the headers phase,
43:  * and a completion handler cancels the call if the job dies mid-body — the
44:  * socket close interrupts the blocking read instead of letting it drain to
45:  * EOF on a dispatcher thread. A read interrupted that way resurfaces as
46:  * [CancellationException].
47:  *
48:  * [action] is suspending so callers can issue a follow-up request (e.g. the
49:  * non-streaming fallback) within the same job's cancellation scope.
50:  */
51: suspend fun <T> Call.executeStreaming(action: suspend (Response) -> T): T {
52:     val job = requireNotNull(coroutineContext[Job]) { "executeStreaming requires a coroutine Job" }
53:     return await().use { response ->
54:         val handle = job.invokeOnCompletion { cause -> if (cause != null) cancel() }
55:         try {
56:             action(response)
57:         } catch (e: IOException) {
58:             if (isCanceled()) {
59:                 throw CancellationException("request cancelled during body read", e)
60:             }
61:             throw e
62:         } finally {
63:             handle.dispose()
64:         }
65:     }
66: }

68: /** True when the response body is actually delivered as an SSE stream. */
69: fun Response.deliversSse(): Boolean = header("Content-Type")?.trim()?.startsWith("text/event-stream", ignoreCase = true) == true

92:  * `\n`, events are dispatched on blank lines, and `event:`/`id:`/`retry:`
93:  * fields and `:` comments are ignored — the AI providers encode everything

97:     val source = body?.source() ?: return
98:     val buffer = StringBuilder()

100:         val line = source.readUtf8Line() ?: break // EOF ends the stream
101:         when {
102:             line.isEmpty() -> {
103:                 if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) {
104:                     onData(buffer.toString())
105:                     buffer.setLength(0)
106:                 }
107:             }
108: 
109:             line.startsWith("data:") -> {
110:                 var data = line.removePrefix("data:")
111:                 if (data.startsWith(" ")) data = data.removePrefix(" ")
112:                 if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) buffer.append('\n')
113:                 buffer.append(data)
114:             }
115: 
116:             // event:, id:, retry: and :comment lines carry no payload here.
117:         }
118:     }
119:     // Flush a trailing event that was not terminated by a blank line.
120:     if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) onData(buffer.toString())
121: }

package com.aistudio.mcpchat.data.network

import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.awaitClose
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.channelFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine
import okhttp3.Call
import okhttp3.Callback
import okhttp3.Response
import java.io.IOException
import kotlin.coroutines.resume
import kotlin.coroutines.resumeWithException

// keep await(), deliversSse(), looksLikeStreamUnsupported()

sealed interface SseStreamEvent {
    /** One complete `data:` field payload from an SSE body. */
    data class Data(val payload: String) : SseStreamEvent
    /** 200 whose body is plain JSON — gateway ignored the stream flag. */
    data class PlainBody(val body: String) : SseStreamEvent
    /** Endpoint rejected streaming (501 / 4xx naming streaming) — retry without it. */
    data class StreamRejected(val code: Int, val errorBody: String) : SseStreamEvent
    /** Any other non-2xx response. */
    data class HttpError(val code: Int, val errorBody: String) : SseStreamEvent
}

fun Call.sseStreamFlow(): Flow<SseStreamEvent> = channelFlow {
    launch(Dispatchers.IO) {
        try {
            val response = await()
            response.use {
                if (!it.isSuccessful) {
                    val errorBody = it.body?.string() ?: ""
                    val event = if (looksLikeStreamUnsupported(it.code, errorBody)) {
                        SseStreamEvent.StreamRejected(it.code, errorBody)
                    } else {
                        SseStreamEvent.HttpError(it.code, errorBody)
                    }
                    send(event)
                    return@launch
                }
                if (!it.deliversSse()) {
                    send(SseStreamEvent.PlainBody(it.body?.string() ?: ""))
                    return@launch
                }
                readSseData(it) { data -> send(SseStreamEvent.Data(data)) }
            }
        } catch (e: IOException) {
            close(e)
        }
    }
    awaitClose { this@sseStreamFlow.cancel() }
}
```

    @Test
    fun `cancelling mid-stream interrupts the throttled SSE body read`() {
        val sseBody = buildString {
            repeat(10) { i ->
                append("""data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":"c$i "}}""")
                    .append("\n\n")
            }
            append("""data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}""").append("\n\n")
            append("""data: {"type":"message_stop"}""").append("\n\n")
        }
        // ~4 bytes per 150ms: a full drain takes ~30s, so only the socket
        // close from call.cancel() can end the read promptly.
        server.enqueue(
            MockResponse().setResponseCode(200)
                .setHeader("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
                .setBody(sseBody)
                .throttleBody(4, 150, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS),
        )

        val start = System.currentTimeMillis()
        runBlocking {
            var cancellation: CancellationException? = null
            val job = launch {
                try {
                    client.streamContent(config, "claude-x", emptyList(), emptyList(), "") {}
                } catch (e: CancellationException) {
                    cancellation = e
                    throw e
                }
            }
            delay(1500)
            job.cancelAndJoin()
            assertNotNull("expected CancellationException from the interrupted read", cancellation)
        }
        val elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis() - start

        // Without the job-tied call.cancel() the read would drain ~30s.
        assertTrue("cancel should interrupt the throttled read promptly (took ${elapsed}ms)", elapsed < 5000)
    }

Cancelling the coroutine cancels the\n * in-flight HTTP request immediately (Stop button) instead of letting a\n * blocking [Call.execute] run to its full timeout on a dispatcher thread.\n */\nsuspend fun Call.await(): Response = suspendCancellableCoroutine { continuation ->\n    enqueue(\n        object : Callback {\n            override fun onResponse(call: Call, response: Response) {\n                continuation.resume(response)\n            }\n\n            override fun onFailure(call: Call, e: IOException) {\n                if (call.isCanceled()) {\n                    // Surface cancellation as CancellationException so\n                    // structured concurrency keeps working.\n                    continuation.cancel(e)\n                } else {\n                    continuation.resumeWithException(e)\n                }\n            }\n        },\n    )\n    continuation.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }\n}\n\n/** True when the response body is actually delivered as an SSE stream. */\nfun Response.deliversSse(): Boolean = header(\"Content-Type\")?.trim()?.startsWith(\"text/event-stream\", ignoreCase = true) == true\n\n/**\n * Heuristic for endpoints that reject streaming outright: 501 Not\n * Implemented, or a 4xx whose body names streaming (\"streaming is not\n * supported\", \"stream mode is disabled\", …). Callers retry the request\n * without `stream:true` / `alt=sse` in that case.\n */\nfun looksLikeStreamUnsupported(code: Int, errorBody: String): Boolean {\n    if (code == 501) return true\n    if (code != 400 && code != 404 && code != 405) return false\n    return errorBody.contains(\"stream\", ignoreCase = true)\n}\n\n/**\n * Terminal or in-flight outcomes of a streaming call, normalizing the\n * transport concerns (SSE framing, fallback detection) away from the\n * provider-specific payload parsing.\n */\nsealed interface SseStreamEvent {\n    /** One complete `data:` field payload from the SSE body. */\n    data class Data(val payload: String) : SseStreamEvent\n\n    /** 200 whose body is plain JSON — the gateway ignored the stream flag. */\n    data class PlainBody(val body: String) : SseStreamEvent\n\n    /** Endpoint rejected streaming outright — retry once without it. */\n    data class StreamRejected(val code: Int, val errorBody: String) : SseStreamEvent\n\n    /** Any other non-2xx response. */\n    data class HttpError(val code: Int, val errorBody: String) : SseStreamEvent\n}\n\n/**\n * Executes the call and exposes its outcome as a cold [Flow]: SSE `data:`\n * events stream as [SseStreamEvent.Data], while non-SSE responses surface as\n * one terminal event each.\n *\n * Structured concurrency replaces the manual job-completion wiring of the\n * old `executeStreaming`: the reader coroutine runs on [Dispatchers.IO],\n * `send` backpressures when the collector falls behind, and [awaitClose]\n * cancels the underlying call the moment the collector goes away — the\n * socket close interrupts the blocking read instead of draining it to EOF\n * on a dispatcher thread.\n */\nfun Call.sseStreamFlow(): Flow<SseStreamEvent> = channelFlow {\n    launch(Dispatchers.IO) {\n        try {\n            val response = await()\n            response.use {\n                if (!it.isSuccessful) {\n                    val errorBody = it.body?.string() ?: \"\"\n                    val event = if (looksLikeStreamUnsupported(it.code, errorBody)) {\n                        SseStreamEvent.StreamRejected(it.code, errorBody)\n                    } else {\n                        SseStreamEvent.HttpError(it.code, errorBody)\n                    }\n                    send(event)\n                } else if (!it.deliversSse()) {\n                    send(SseStreamEvent.PlainBody(it.body?.string() ?: \"\"))\n                } else {\n                    it.readSseData { data -> send(SseStreamEvent.Data(data)) }\n                }\n            }\n            close()\n        } catch (e: IOException) {\n            close(e)\n        }\n    }\n    // Runs on collector cancellation AND on normal completion (no-op for a\n    // finished call) — either way the call never outlives the flow.\n    awaitClose { this@sseStreamFlow.cancel() }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parses an SSE body and hands each complete `data:` field value to [onData]\n * as it arrives. Handles the spec essentials: multi-line `data:` fields are\n * joined with `\\n`, events dispatch on blank lines, and `event:`/`id:`/\n * `retry:` fields and `:` comments are ignored — the AI providers encode\n * everything in `data:` payloads.\n */\nprivate suspend fun Response.readSseData(onData: suspend (String) -> Unit) {\n    val source = body?.source() ?: return\n    val buffer = StringBuilder()\n    while (true) {\n        val line = source.readUtf8Line() ?: break // EOF ends the stream\n        when {\n            line.isEmpty() -> {\n                if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) {\n                    onData(buffer.toString())\n                    buffer.setLength(0)\n                }\n            }\n\n            line.startsWith(\"data:\") -> {\n                var data = line.removePrefix(\"data:\")\n                if (data.startsWith(\" \")) data = data.removePrefix(\" \")\n                if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) buffer.append('\\n')\n                buffer.append(data)\n            }\n\n            // event:, id:, retry: and :comment lines carry no payload here.\n        }\n    }\n    // Flush a trailing event that was not terminated by a blank line.\n    if (buffer.isNotEmpty()) onData(buffer.toString())\n}\n",

```kotlin
private suspend fun executeFunctionCalls(
    functionCalls: List<GeminiPart.FunctionCall>,
    toolNameToToolMap: Map<String, McpTool>,
    sanitizedToOriginalName: Map<String, String>,
    serverMap: Map<String, McpServer>,
    accumulatedToolCalls: MutableList<McpToolCall>,
    onToolCallUpdate: ((List<McpToolCall>) -> Unit)?,
): List<GeminiPart> = supervisorScope {
    val progressLock = Any()

    val preparedCalls = functionCalls.map { fc ->
        prepareToolCall(fc, toolNameToToolMap, sanitizedToOriginalName, serverMap)
    }
    synchronized(progressLock) {
        accumulatedToolCalls.addAll(preparedCalls.map { it.toolCall })
        onToolCallUpdate?.invoke(accumulatedToolCalls.toList())
    }

    // Tool calls issued together in one hop are independent by definition —
    // run them concurrently. supervisorScope + per-call isolation keeps one
    // failure from cancelling siblings, and await() order preserves the
    // call↔response pairing strict providers require.
    val jobs = preparedCalls.map { prepared ->
        async {
            val outcome = runPreparedToolCall(prepared)
            synchronized(progressLock) {
                replaceToolCall(accumulatedToolCalls, prepared.toolCall.callId, outcome.completed)
                onToolCallUpdate?.invoke(accumulatedToolCalls.toList())
            }
            outcome.response
        }
    }
    jobs.forEach { it.join() }
    jobs.map { it.await() }
}
```

If job failed with unexpected Throwable (shouldn't — isolation catches Exception... but Errors like OOM propagate) → join returns; await throws it; remaining jobs already joined (all done) → no sibling cancellation ✓ — this is exactly the supervisor isolation.

```kotlin
private fun prepareToolCall(
    fc: GeminiPart.FunctionCall,
    toolNameToToolMap: Map<String, McpTool>,
    sanitizedToOriginalName: Map<String, String>,
    serverMap: Map<String, McpServer>,
): PreparedToolCall {
    val originalToolName = toolNameToToolMap[fc.name]?.name
        ?: sanitizedToOriginalName[fc.name]
    val toolDef = originalToolName?.let { toolNameToToolMap[it] }
    val server = toolDef?.let { def -> serverMap[def.serverId] }
    return PreparedToolCall(
        fc = fc,
        resolvedToolName = originalToolName ?: fc.name,
        server = server,
        toolCall = McpToolCall(
            callId = UUID.randomUUID().toString(),
            serverId = server?.id ?: "unknown",
            serverName = server?.name ?: "Remote MCP Server",
            toolName = originalToolName ?: fc.name,
            inputArguments = fc.args,
            status = ToolExecutionStatus.EXECUTING,
            thoughtSignature = fc.thoughtSignature,
        ),
    )
}
```

```kotlin
private data class ToolCallOutcome(
    val completed: McpToolCall,
    val response: GeminiPart.FunctionResponse,
)

private suspend fun runPreparedToolCall(prepared: PreparedToolCall): ToolCallOutcome {
    val execResult: String
    val isSuccess: Boolean
    val latencyMs: Long
    val errorMessage: String?
    try {
        if (prepared.server == null) {
            // Guard unknown tool (provider hallucinated a name or server was
            // disabled after tool discovery) — fail fast without calling MCP.
            execResult = JSONObject()
                .put("error", "Unknown tool '${prepared.resolvedToolName}' — no enabled MCP server provides this tool")
                .toString()
            isSuccess = false
            latencyMs = 0
            errorMessage = "Unknown tool"
        } else {
            val (result, logItem) = mcpRepository.executeTool(prepared.server, prepared.resolvedToolName, prepared.fc.args)
            execResult = result
            isSuccess = logItem.isSuccess
            latencyMs = logItem.latencyMs
            errorMessage = logItem.errorMessage
        }
    } catch (e: CancellationException) {
        throw e
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        // Isolation: an unexpected failure is reported as this call's error
        // result; sibling calls keep running.
        execResult = JSONObject().put("error", "Tool execution failed: ${e.message}").toString()
        isSuccess = false
        latencyMs = 0
        errorMessage = e.message ?: e.javaClass.simpleName
    }
    val completed = prepared.toolCall.copy(
        outputResult = execResult,
        isSuccess = isSuccess,
        status = if (isSuccess) ToolExecutionStatus.SUCCESS else ToolExecutionStatus.ERROR,
        executionTimeMs = latencyMs,
        errorMessage = errorMessage,
    )
    return ToolCallOutcome(
        completed = completed,
        response = GeminiPart.FunctionResponse(
            name = prepared.fc.name,
            response = parseResultToMap(execResult),
            thoughtSignature = prepared.fc.thoughtSignature,
        ),
    )
}

`runPreparedToolCall` declares `val execResult: String` etc. and assigns in try/catch — Kotlin doesn't allow definite-assignment via multiple branches assigning vals... actually you CAN assign a `val` exactly once in different branches, but here I assign in try AND in catch AND possibly read — the pattern "val x: T; try { x = ... } catch { x = ... }" IS allowed with definite assignment... hmm no: `val execResult: String` followed by assignment inside try block — that's allowed if compiler proves exactly-one assignment... Actually Kotlin allows `val x: Int; if (c) x = 1 else x = 2` ✓. But assignment inside try{} where an exception could occur AFTER partial assignment? Each branch assigns all 4 vals exactly once and both paths cover. Kotlin's definite assignment for try/catch: assignments in try are NOT considered definitely assigned after (exception could occur before assignment) — the catch assigns them, and after try-catch... the compiler historically doesn't track this well — that's the error.

Fix: convert to a single immutable result via a helper that returns a data holder:
